name: Scanned PDF Tables → Excel
tagline: Scanned or text, a PDF's tables come out as Excel — OCR runs on your device.
description:
Scanned PDF Tables → Excel turns a PDF's tables into a real Excel file — one sheet per page — entirely on your own device.

IT READS PHOTOCOPIES. A scanned page is just a picture: there is no text in it to extract. This app renders the page and actually reads it — finding the words, reading them, and recovering the row-and-column grid rather than a wall of text. It runs on your graphics chip when you have one, and on the processor where you don't. It tells you which one ran.

IT STILL READS TEXT PDFs EXACTLY. Page by page, it checks whether there is real text. If there is, it reads the numbers instead of guessing at them. That matters for SERFF insurance rate and rule filings, which is what this was built for: they arrive as digital rate tables with scanned exhibits bound in, and you want each page handled the right way. Sheets are labelled, so a reading of a picture is not mistaken for an exact one later.

HONEST ABOUT LIMITS. Reading a picture is a reading, not a transcript: a faint, skewed or handwritten page will come back imperfect, and you should check the numbers that matter. Where it cannot see a table, the app lays the text out by position instead and says so.

Everything needed to read a page is packed inside the app. There is no download after install. The filing you drop in, and the spreadsheet that comes out, stays on this device.

Its smaller sibling, PDF Tables → Excel, stays the tiny text-only option if you never touch scans.
